name: Rohit Mukherjee
description: Rohit Mukherjee, Alexander von Humboldt postdoctoral fellow at the Institute for Theoretical Physics, University of Cologne. Nonequilibrium quantum many-body physics and statistical mechanics of quantum error correction.
home: I am an Alexander von Humboldt postdoctoral fellow at the Institute for Theoretical Physics, University of Cologne, working with Simon Trebst.

Before coming to Cologne I was a Fulbright fellow at Cornell University (2023–2025), working with Debanjan Chowdhury. I did my PhD and MSc in physics at IIT Kanpur, advised by Arijit Kundu and Avinash Singh, and my BSc at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Centenary College, Kolkata.

I work on nonequilibrium quantum many-body physics and on the statistical mechanics of quantum error correction. On the dynamics side, I study dynamical freezing and Floquet thermalization in periodically driven systems, and how freezing can be used in superconducting circuits. On the error-correction side, I study Nishimori criticality, Bayesian inference and the decoding of Zq surface codes. I am also interested in optimal control of quantum processors.

My tools are exact diagonalization, tensor networks (MPS, MPO, TEBD, TDVP) and hybrid Monte Carlo–tensor-network methods. Earlier I worked on magnon transport and thermal Hall effects in quantum magnets, Schwinger-boson theory of chiral spin models, Weyl semimetals, and iridate heterostructures.
